item.title: Drill 2026-10-21: decode (GS-relative PEB load)
item.description:
Decode one instruction (Windows x64)
Decode this instruction:
``` 65 48 8B 04 25 60 00 00 00 ```
What is the assembly? What does the `65` byte do, and why is there a SIB byte when no register is used for the address?
ANSWER: `mov rax, qword ptr gs:[0x60]`
- `65` is the GS segment-override prefix; `48` is REX.W (64-bit operand); `8B` = MOV r64, r/m64. ModRM `04` = `00 000 100`: mod=00, reg=rax, rm=100 (SIB follows). - SIB `25` = `00 100 101`: index=100 means "no index", base=101 with mod=00 means "no base, disp32 only". That is the only way to encode an absolute address in 64-bit mode (plain mod=00 rm=101 is RIP-relative). disp32 = `60 00 00 00` = 0x60. - On Windows x64, GS points at the TEB, and TEB+0x60 holds the PEB pointer, so this loads the PEB address into rax (shellcode and malware use it to walk loaded modules).
